content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'd like to know how many [product_name] devices can be connected to a PC using MODBUS TCP/IP communication. Specifically, is it possible to connect 22 [product_name] devices to one PC only for data transfer? If this isn't feasible, does anyone have alternative suggestions? Best regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], please use English in the forum. If you wish to communicate in another language, please do so via private message. Also, the answer provided earlier is not entirely correct. The [product_name] with [article_no] can handle up to 16 connections, although only 8 of these are static connections.
A new question published by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled 'Does [article_no] support Modbus TCP/IP ?'. Best regards, [user_name]_Moderator

Hello, If your PC has a Modbus TCP/IP Client, you can use Modbus communication with as many [product_name] devices as your software can support. If you're asking how many Modbus devices you can connect to a single [product_name], then: you can connect one Modbus device to each of the 8 static connections (either Client or Server). Additionally, the [product_name] provides a dynamic Server mode, allowing you to connect 8 more Modbus devices, as long as these devices are Modbus TCP/IP Clients. Hope this information helps.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion focuses on the maximum number of [product_name] devices that can be connected via MODBUS TCP/IP to a PC for data collection. Users are confused about limitations due to a lack of clarity in documentation regarding static and dynamic connections. There's uncertainty about whether 8 or 16 connections are supported, and how this limit applies based on whether the PC or the [product_name] is acting as the client or server.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish to connect and communicate with at least 22 [product_name] devices simultaneously via PC using MODBUS TCP/IP for straightforward data acquisition, ideally without complicated configuration or workarounds.
